issue_context.title: Extract smartthings switch energy attributes into sensors
issue_context.body:
This issue is for the switch platform of the smartthings integration.

The switch integration has embedded sensors for energy usage. This is no longer the preferred approach. Integrations using this approach should turn this data into standalone sensors.

This is important because Home Assistant is going to introduce home energy management (HEM) in 2021.8. HEM will be able to consume the data if it is exposed as standalone sensors.

To make sure that the sensors that represent total kWh is usable for HEM, set `state_class` to `measurement` and set `last_reset` to the timestamp of when the meter got reset (midnight if daily etc). [See sensor documentation for more information.](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor)

[Link to the architecture discussion.](https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/discussions/579)
comments:
Hey there @andrewsayre, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`smartthings`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L459) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

There's two other areas to update:

- [ ] The Climate platform also embeds energy attributes from the capabilities `powerConsumptionReport` and `demandResponseLoadControl` that need to be removed.
- [ ] The Sensor platform will represent the SmartThings power-related capabilities as discrete entities once removed from the `switch` and `climate` platforms based on how the code works today, but logic needs to be added to set the desired property values (`state_class` and `last_reset`)
Note that this can be implemend in 2 phases: 1) add new entities and 2) remove the old properties.
